run_rule.action_limit: Synthetic provider state, intercepted synthetic direct OAuth requests and isolated disposable PostgreSQL schemas only. No normal profile/database, live account, real recipient, deploy or push.

FENCE.evidence: Old connection cannot execute, poll or drain queued work before consent. All failed attempts preserve original saved state/events.

REPLACE.evidence: Success leaves one usable replacement under original local connection ID, preserves watch preference, resets old cursor/trigger and discards obsolete queued work. Two Gmail accounts are independently reconnected.

FAILURE.evidence: Cancellation, authorize failure, wrong email, wrong owner, unknown identity, foreign target, stale/superseded callbacks, early supersession, expiry, disconnect and duplicate current account are fenced. Persisted claimed callback is never retried after restart; fresh consent succeeds.

NOLEGACY.evidence: Ordinary generic connect route and current provider are used; fixture rejects all old project session restoration, reconnect, remote grant/trigger deletion and execution.

SECRET.evidence: This service-only fixture contains no renderer/sandbox settings or actual managed HTTP transport. The frozen applicability subject is exercised by CP03.v2, which independently validates actual composition/settings and signed requests; this evaluator does not infer that boundary from synthetic provider responses.

GRANT.evidence: Old remote grant remains untouched. Newly completed owned orphan is deleted after wrong email, disconnect or early supersession; foreign/unverified or locally retained grants are not deleted.
